meta.name: FarmShare USA — Chatbot Knowledge Base
meta.voice: Warm, encouraging, plain-spoken, second person. Optimistic and capable — independence not fear. Never doom, prepper, or political.
meta.notes: Starter knowledge base built from current project materials. Prices, tiers, and launch status are placeholders that should be kept in sync with config/site.ts and the live pages. When unsure, the bot should point users to /contact.
meta.fallback: I'm not totally sure on that one yet — but I don't want to guess. You can reach the FarmShare USA team directly at the Contact page and they'll take care of you.

qa.question: What is FarmShare USA?
qa.answer: FarmShare USA is the operating system for modern self-sufficiency. We give you the tools, step-by-step systems, and a nationwide community to grow your own food, build independent systems, and connect with local farm co-ops — wherever you live.

qa.question: Who is FarmShare USA for?
qa.answer: It's for anyone who wants more control over their food — city and suburban beginners, aspiring homesteaders, small landowners with 1–5 acres, and people who want to build or join local food co-ops. Start where you are, no experience required.

qa.question: Is FarmShare USA political or a prepper thing?
qa.answer: No. We're about independence, not isolation — resilience, not fear. The tone here is optimistic and practical: growing real food and building community. No politics, no doom.

qa.question: What makes FarmShare USA different from a gardening blog or YouTube channel?
qa.answer: Most content teaches in scattered pieces. We give you structured, sequenced systems plus a co-op network and a community for accountability — transformation and implementation, not just information.

qa.question: Do I need land to use FarmShare USA?
qa.answer: Not at all. Our plans work from a city balcony to five suburban acres. We'll meet you wherever you are and help you make the most of your space.

qa.question: I live in an apartment — can this still work for me?
qa.answer: Yes. Container growing, balcony setups, and connecting with nearby co-ops all work without a yard. The free 30-Day Plan includes a layout that works on a balcony.

qa.question: What's the mission?
qa.answer: To be the hub for modern homesteading — the tools, knowledge, and community to live independently, grow naturally, and reduce reliance on industrial food systems.

qa.question: How do I get started?
qa.answer: The easiest first step is the free 30-Day Self-Sufficient Backyard Plan. Grab it, plant your first bed, and explore co-ops near you from there.

qa.question: Is FarmShare USA available in all 50 states?
qa.answer: Yes — the plans, courses, and community work anywhere in the country, and we're growing the co-op network state by state. If your area is light on co-ops today, you can be one of the first to list one.

qa.question: Is this a movement I can be part of?
qa.answer: Absolutely — that's the heart of it. Thousands of families are building food independence together, and you can join free and grow into it at your own pace.

qa.question: What is the 30-Day Self-Sufficient Backyard Plan?
qa.answer: It's our free starter plan: a day-by-day planting calendar for your zone, the exact starter crops that won't fail, and a layout that works on a balcony or an acre.

qa.question: Is the 30-Day Plan really free?
qa.answer: Yes, completely free. Just enter your email and we'll send it over, along with a short 5-day starter series to help you get going.

qa.question: What do I get when I download the 30-Day Plan?
qa.answer: A planting calendar tailored to your growing zone, a fail-proof starter crop list, and a simple space layout — plus a 5-day email series to walk you through your first steps.

qa.question: Do I need any experience to start?
qa.answer: None at all. Everything is sequenced so you never feel lost — we start with the basics and build from there.

qa.question: Will the plan work in my climate or growing zone?
qa.answer: Yes — the planting calendar is built to adapt to your zone so you're planting the right things at the right time for where you live.

qa.question: How much time does it take each day?
qa.answer: Just a little. The plan is designed to fit a busy life — small, doable steps that add up to a real harvest over 30 days.

qa.question: What happens after I sign up?
qa.answer: You'll get the 30-Day Plan and a 5-day starter series by email. From there you can explore membership, courses, and the co-op directory whenever you're ready.

qa.question: Can I really grow food in my first season?
qa.answer: Yes. The plan focuses on reliable starter crops so you can harvest real food in your first season — start where you are, this season.

qa.question: Is there a free membership?
qa.answer: Yes. The Free plan ($0) gives you the weekly almanac and access to the co-op directory — a great way to start with no commitment.

qa.question: What membership tiers are there?
qa.answer: Four: Free ($0), Grower ($19/mo), Homesteader ($59/mo), and Steward ($199/mo). You can start free and upgrade anytime.

qa.question: What does the Grower plan include?
qa.answer: Grower ($19/mo) unlocks the full course library, guides, and the member forum — ideal once you're ready to go beyond the basics.

qa.question: What does the Homesteader plan include?
qa.answer: Homesteader ($59/mo) adds land and plot design templates, live workshops, and the co-op toolkit on top of everything in Grower.

qa.question: What does the Steward plan include?
qa.answer: Steward ($199/mo) is our top tier — it includes 1:1 homestead design and vendor introductions, for people who want hands-on guidance.

qa.question: Is there a discount for paying annually?
qa.answer: Yes — choosing annual billing saves you about 20% compared to paying monthly.

qa.question: Can I cancel anytime?
qa.answer: Yes, you can cancel anytime — no long-term lock-in.

qa.question: What is a Founding Member?
qa.answer: Founding Member is our early-supporter highlight on the Homesteader tier — a way to get in early as the movement grows. Join the waitlist to be among the first.

qa.question: Can I upgrade or downgrade later?
qa.answer: Yes — start on any plan and move up or down as your needs change.

qa.question: When does checkout open?
qa.answer: Paid checkout is opening soon. For now you can join the waitlist so you're first in line when it goes live.

qa.question: Do I have to pay to find or join co-ops?
qa.answer: No — the co-op directory is available on the Free plan. You can search and connect without a paid membership.

qa.question: What's the difference between the free and paid plans?
qa.answer: Free gives you the weekly almanac and the co-op directory. Paid plans add courses, guides, the forum, design templates, workshops, and (at the top tier) 1:1 design help.

qa.question: How will I pay — what methods are accepted?
qa.answer: Checkout is opening soon and will support standard secure payment methods. Join the waitlist and we'll share details as it launches.

qa.question: Is my membership good for my whole family?
qa.answer: Our plans are designed to help your whole household build food independence together. Specific multi-user details will be confirmed at launch — reach out anytime via Contact.

qa.question: What courses does FarmShare USA offer?
qa.answer: We offer a growing course library covering food production, systems, animals, land use, and more — with our flagship 8-week Food Independence Blueprint at the center.

qa.question: What is the Food Independence Blueprint?
qa.answer: It's our flagship 8-week program that takes you from grocery-store dependence to a self-sufficient food system, with a 30/60/90-day roadmap to put it all into action.

qa.question: How long is the Food Independence Blueprint?
qa.answer: Eight weeks — covering the food system and planning, growing basics, production systems, scaling, protein, water and sustainability, preservation, and your personal independence plan.

qa.question: What will I learn in the Blueprint?
qa.answer: Week by week: food-system reality and planning, growing basics, production systems, scaling output, protein systems, water and sustainability, preservation, and building your 30/60/90-day independence plan.

qa.question: How much does the Food Independence Blueprint cost?
qa.answer: There are three options: Entry ($99), Standard ($199), and Premium with coaching ($499). You can pick the level of support that fits you.

qa.question: What's the difference between the Blueprint pricing tiers?
qa.answer: Entry ($99) is the core program, Standard ($199) adds more depth and resources, and Premium ($499) includes coaching for hands-on guidance.

qa.question: Do I get bonuses with the Blueprint?
qa.answer: Yes — bonuses include a garden planner, a chicken guide, and land layout templates to speed up your results.

qa.question: Is there a free webinar or preview?
qa.answer: Yes — we offer a webinar, "How to Build a Self-Sufficient Food System in 90 Days," as a great way to preview the approach before enrolling.

qa.question: Do I keep access to the course?
qa.answer: The Blueprint is built to be your long-term reference as you put the system in place. Exact access details are confirmed at enrollment — reach out via Contact if you'd like specifics.

qa.question: Are the courses good for beginners?
qa.answer: Yes. Everything is sequenced step by step, so even a complete beginner can follow along and take action with confidence.

qa.question: Are courses included in membership?
qa.answer: The full course library is included starting with the Grower plan ($19/mo). The flagship Blueprint program is also available on its own.

qa.question: Can I get coaching or 1:1 help?
qa.answer: Yes — the Premium Blueprint tier ($499) includes coaching, and the Steward membership ($199/mo) includes 1:1 homestead design.

qa.question: What is a farm co-op?
qa.answer: A farm co-op is a local network where neighbors grow, trade, share, and buy food together. It's a way to access fresh local food and build community — independence, together.

qa.question: How do I find a co-op near me?
qa.answer: Use the co-op directory — search by ZIP or state and filter by consumer or provider to see what's growing near you.

qa.question: What's the difference between a consumer and a provider?
qa.answer: A consumer joins to access local food; a provider grows or supplies food to the network. You can filter the directory by either role.

qa.question: How do I list or start my own co-op?
qa.answer: You can list your co-op right from the directory page using the "List your co-op" option — a great way to put your area on the map.

qa.question: What do co-ops offer?
qa.answer: It varies by co-op — commonly eggs, produce, raw honey, and other local goods — plus the chance to trade, share, and connect with growers near you.

qa.question: Are the co-ops vetted?
qa.answer: We're building a network of vetted growers and providers under the FarmShare USA Certified standard so you can connect with confidence.

qa.question: There are no co-ops in my area — what now?
qa.answer: You can be one of the first to list one and help your community get started. The network grows as members like you put their area on the map.

qa.question: Does it cost anything to join a co-op?
qa.answer: The directory is free to search on the Free plan. Individual co-ops set their own terms for joining — you'll see details on each listing.

qa.question: Can I sell what I grow through a co-op?
qa.answer: Yes — as a provider you can connect with consumers and other growers in your area. List your co-op or provider profile to get started.

qa.question: Why are co-ops a big part of FarmShare USA?
qa.answer: Local networks make food independence realistic and resilient. Aggregating co-ops nationwide is one of the things that makes FarmShare USA more than a content brand.

qa.question: What are FarmShare USA Certified Vendors?
qa.answer: They're vetted businesses in the FarmShare USA marketplace — tools, seeds, equipment, butchers, processing, contractors, and more — that you can trust for your homestead.

qa.question: What kinds of vendors can I find?
qa.answer: Categories include tools, seeds, and equipment, plus trades like butchers, deer/meat processing, farm equipment, and contractors.

qa.question: How do I become a certified vendor?
qa.answer: You can apply to join the certified vendor directory — head to the Vendors page or Contact us to start the application.

qa.question: Are vendors vetted?
qa.answer: Yes — the FarmShare USA Certified mark means a vendor has been vetted, so you can shop and hire with confidence.

qa.question: How do I find a vendor near me?
qa.answer: Browse the certified vendor directory and filter by category to find tools, seeds, equipment, and trades that fit your needs.

qa.question: Do you sell products directly?
qa.answer: We connect you with vetted vendors and partners rather than being a single store, so you can find the right tools, seeds, and services for your project.

qa.question: What is FarmShare USA Health?
qa.answer: It's our health hub where clinical professionals share the benefits of homesteading and growing your own food, plus vetted products and services.

qa.question: Are the health professionals credentialed?
qa.answer: Yes — the Health section features clinical professionals, so the guidance comes from credible, qualified voices.

qa.question: Is the health content medical advice?
qa.answer: It's educational information about the benefits of growing your own food and healthier living — not a substitute for personalized medical advice from your own provider.

qa.question: What does the Health hub offer?
qa.answer: Professional perspectives on the health benefits of homesteading and home-grown food, plus vetted products and services to support a healthier lifestyle.

qa.question: Why does a homesteading site cover health?
qa.answer: Because growing your own food is one of the most powerful things you can do for your family's health — better quality, freshness, and connection to what you eat.

qa.question: What is the FarmShare USA community?
qa.answer: It's where the movement lives — groups, forums, and people who get it, so you have support and accountability as you build your food independence.

qa.question: Is the community free?
qa.answer: There's a free way in, with more unlocked on paid tiers (like the member forum on Grower). The community is designed to welcome you wherever you start.

qa.question: What do paid tiers unlock in the community?
qa.answer: Paid plans add things like the member forum, live workshops, and founding-cohort groups — deeper access and connection as you grow.

qa.question: How do I join the community?
qa.answer: Start by grabbing the free 30-Day Plan or joining the Free plan — both connect you to the movement, with more community features as you upgrade.

qa.question: What can I expect from the community?
qa.answer: Encouragement, real answers from people doing the same thing, and accountability that keeps you going when motivation runs thin.

qa.question: What is Homestead Acquisition & Design?
qa.answer: It's our consulting offering for land-buying guidance, property layout and design, and farm-startup planning — for people ready to build something bigger.

qa.question: Can you help me buy land?
qa.answer: Yes — our Homestead Acquisition & Design service includes guidance on buying the right land for your goals.

qa.question: Can you help design my property?
qa.answer: Yes — we help with property layout and design so you can make the most of your land, whether it's a quarter-acre or several acres.

qa.question: Who is the design consulting for?
qa.answer: It's ideal for small landowners and aspiring homesteaders who want expert help planning land use, systems, and a farm startup.

qa.question: How do I get started with consulting?
qa.answer: You can apply or reach out through the Homestead Design page or Contact, and we'll talk through your goals and next steps.

qa.question: Is 1:1 design available with membership?
qa.answer: Yes — the Steward membership ($199/mo) includes 1:1 homestead design and vendor introductions.

qa.question: What is the Learn / Almanac section?
qa.answer: It's our growing field library of articles and guides — organized by what you're trying to do (start a bed, design acres, raise a flock, build a co-op), not by date.

qa.question: Is the Learn content free?
qa.answer: Yes — the Learn library is a free, growing reference to help you take action wherever you are.

qa.question: What topics does Learn cover?
qa.answer: Food independence, beginner-friendly guides, land use for 1–5 acres, animals, systems, co-ops, income, and lifestyle — all in plain language.

qa.question: Can I request a topic?
qa.answer: We'd love that — reach out through Contact and tell us what you want to learn. Reader questions help shape the library.

qa.question: I'm a total beginner — where do I start?
qa.answer: Start with the free 30-Day Plan. It tells you exactly what to plant first for your zone, so you skip the overwhelm and get a real harvest fast.

qa.question: What are the best first crops to grow?
qa.answer: The 30-Day Plan includes a fail-proof starter crop list chosen to be forgiving and productive — the exact crops that won't let a beginner down.

qa.question: How do I grow food without a yard?
qa.answer: Containers, balconies, and vertical setups all work — and our plans include layouts for small spaces. You can also tap into local co-ops for fresh food.

qa.question: Where do I start with raising chickens?
qa.answer: The Blueprint's protein systems and the bonus chicken guide walk you through getting started with a small flock the right way.

qa.question: How do I set up water systems?
qa.answer: Water and sustainability is a core week in the Food Independence Blueprint — it covers building systems that keep producing reliably.

qa.question: How do I preserve my harvest?
qa.answer: Food preservation is a dedicated week in the Blueprint, so you can store what you grow and eat from your garden year-round.

qa.question: Can I make income from a small piece of land?
qa.answer: Yes — making the most of 1–5 acres for income is a focus of our land-use guidance and the co-op network, where you can sell or trade what you grow.

qa.question: How much space do I really need?
qa.answer: Less than you think. People grow meaningful food on balconies and quarter-acre lots — our plans scale from a balcony to five acres.

qa.question: What about raised beds?
qa.answer: Raised beds are a great beginner-friendly option, and our layouts and guides show you how to set them up for a productive first season.

qa.question: How do I make the most of 1–5 acres?
qa.answer: Land optimization is one of our specialties — from layout and systems to income. The Homesteader plan's templates and the design consulting go deep here.

qa.question: How do I contact FarmShare USA?
qa.answer: Head to the Contact page and send us a note — we're happy to help with anything about membership, co-ops, vendors, or getting started.

qa.question: Is my email safe? Do you spam?
qa.answer: Your email is safe — no spam, and you can unsubscribe anytime. We only send things that help you on your journey.

qa.question: Is FarmShare USA legit?
qa.answer: Yes. We're a real movement helping families build food independence with structured systems, a vetted co-op and vendor network, and a supportive community. Start free and see for yourself.

qa.question: How do I unsubscribe from emails?
qa.answer: Every email includes an unsubscribe link, so you're always in control. You can opt out anytime.

qa.question: Who founded FarmShare USA?
qa.answer: You can read about the founders and the story behind the movement on the About page.

qa.question: How can I partner with or sponsor FarmShare USA?
qa.answer: We're open to partnerships, vendors, and sponsors — reach out via Contact and let's talk.

qa.question: Do you have a newsletter?
qa.answer: Yes — the free weekly almanac. Grab the 30-Day Plan or join Free and you'll start receiving it.

qa.question: Can I gift a membership or course?
qa.answer: We're finalizing gifting options. In the meantime, reach out via Contact and we'll help you arrange it.

qa.question: What if I need help deciding which plan is right for me?
qa.answer: Tell me a bit about your space and goals and I can point you the right way — or start free with the 30-Day Plan and grow from there. You can also reach the team via Contact.

qa.question: How do I talk to a real person?
qa.answer: Anytime — the Contact page connects you with the FarmShare USA team for anything I can't answer here.
